correctness.rationale: For prime powers v(q^e)<=q^e and v(q^(e+f))<=v(q^e)+v(q^f) by the three exponent cases, so v(ac)<=v(a)+v(c) and v(n)<=n. For odd composite m>=21, factor m=ac with a,c odd >=3; (a-2)(c-2)>=4 implies a+c<=m/2, so v(m)<=m/2. For p odd in even base, the reversal s is odd and <2p because the last digit of p is odd and its leading odd digit d satisfies 2d>=b. If s is a different prime, v(s)=s !=p; if odd composite >=21, v(s)<=s/2<p. The only smaller odd composites 9 and 15 yield v=5 and 8; 15 cannot match a prime, and reversal of p=5 is never 9 in even bases. The only even prime 2 is inadmissible or single-digit. Binary follows. Replayed finite verifier complements rather than replaces proof.

value.rationale: The 2024 foundational general-base study explicitly poses existence of prime v-palindromes by base (Problem 1). This theorem resolves the entire base-2 prime case for arbitrary digit length while leaving known composite binary v-palindromes intact, and establishes a uniform infinite family of parity/leading-digit exclusions for every even base. It distinguishes the permitted prime examples (e.g. 109 in base16) from a provably forbidden natural digit stratum, giving a structural rather than a finite-table observation.
